claim: Development check on a public case: it decides whether an unseen-case test is worth running.

declaration.claim_scope: development only: one public case, one rule (L3, unchanged), one Actor (Haiku 5.5 on the API); not an unseen-case result and not a policy
declaration.decision_rule: development go or no-go, fixed now: PROCEED to an unseen-case comparison of the two presentations if Q has at most half as many trials with a block as E, no slip, and no more side-effect trials than E; otherwise STOP and write it up
declaration.expected_cost: about $0.10 of API money (24 trials at about $0.004) and about 6 minutes
declaration.name: advice-presentation-dev-1-2026-11-15
declaration.purpose: A development check, under the owner's instruction of 2026-11-14 ('If you want to add more things, add more code, do more tests, and do more verification, just do it'), of the requirement presentation of advice (commit 0a817d8) before any unseen-case test of it.
declaration.question: On dev-5, the development case the rule was built from, does showing the L3 rule's advice as the report gate's requirement (Q) cut the trials where the agent still proposes a report the gate refuses, compared with the advice shown as an expectation (E)?
readouts: per arm over its 12 trials: trials with a blocked report (primary), slips (the target finding), side effects (the rule acted and the trial has a conformance finding, a legacy violation, a false belief or no report), correct refusals, trials shown advice, model calls
trials with a block, Q against E, with a two-sided Fisher exact p-value as description
stop_rules: E runs first; an INFRA_ERROR trial or a billing message in E stops the launch before Q
the ledger refuses any call past the process cap
one run per arm: no rerun and no change to the rule, the arms or the read-outs after a result

title: Advice presentation dev 1
